findings_qualitative.value: Velocity dispersion is uniform across the host with modest shear, implying a turbulent ISM

evidence.quote: the high dispersion-to-shear ratio suggests an extremely turbulent ISM

claims.hypothesis: Is the ISM of W2246-0526 turbulent and uniform?
claims.result: FWHM 500-600 km/s across region, shear ~150 km/s
claims.finding: highly turbulent, not a relaxed disk

evidence.quote: There is a strikingly uniform, broad velocity dispersion

claims.finding: comparable only to the most obscured local nuclei

evidence.quote: this ratio is still only matched in the most obscured nuclei of local dusty IR-luminous systems

claims.hypothesis: Is the AGN blowing out the gas isotropically?
claims.experiment: Compare L_bol with momentum- and energy-driven limits
claims.result: L_bol at least twice threshold even for f_g~1

evidence.quote: suggesting that the AGN is likely blowing away all the gas from the galaxy

limitations_admitted.value: Line window missed part of the red wing

evidence.quote: was observed in a spectral window that missed part of the red wing of the line

referee_caveats_inferred: Single short observation; blow-out inference relies on an assumed gas fraction and efficiency
No kinematic modelling; sigma may include beam smearing and unresolved AGN-driven components

reproducibility.score_reason: Single public dataset and simple analysis, but processing details are sparse.
